title: Fault Vector Index: Trace‑Anchor Playground and Error Attribution Pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a lightweight Fault Vector Index (FVI) and a Trace‑Anchor Playground that turns raw traces + logs into a browsable, queryable error taxonomy for oncall and SRE teams. The FVI will normalize and tag failures (timeout, overload/backpressure, model-reject, kv-cache miss, HTTP/gRPC status classes) and attach a causal vector to each request so dashboards and playbooks can surface root cause candidates quickly.

Scope: implement runtime span hooks (low overhead) to emit an error_anchor event, extend our ingestion pipeline to enrich traces and logs with failure_reason tags, store normalized vectors in our OLAP table, and build a Grafana / internal web UI for interactive drilldown (Trace‑Anchor Playground). This work focuses on inference‑path failures (model and serving runtime) and HTTP/gRPC surface errors; infra/networking faults will be linked but treated separately.

Why: current dashboards show symptom metrics (latency, 5xx counts) but lack causal grouping. Teams spend too long correlating traces + model logs during incidents. The FVI reduces MTTR by surfacing ranked failure causes and enabling quick replay/annotation for postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits error_anchor spans for >95% of failure paths (timeouts, model_reject, overload, 4xx/5xx/gRPC codes).
Ingestion pipeline normalizes anchors and populates the fvi_events table with schema: request_id, timestamp, failure_vector, primary_reason, secondary_reasons, model_version, route, region.
Grafana dashboard 'Fault Vector Index Overview' with: breakdown by primary_reason, time-series trend, and top-N routes for each reason.
Trace‑Anchor Playground UI that links a selected FVI row to the full trace and allows annotating primary_reason (saved to incident notes).
Oncall runbook templates auto-populate from primary_reason to suggested remediation steps.
Sampling and storage cost estimates validated: <15% increase in daily ES/OLAP storage and <2% added request latency from span hooks under p95 load.
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Kickoff with SRE, runtime, and telemetry teams. Agreed on minimal span fields (anchor_type, anchor_code, anchor_message, request_id, kv_cache_hit).

2025-02-15: Prototype span hook committed to branch runtime/error-anchor (PR #4521). Hook appends lightweight anchor event to trace without blocking token generation.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/4521

2025-02-20: Ingestion design doc posted to Confluence; chose Kafka topic 'fvi-events' -> Flink enrichment -> ClickHouse ingest. Cost analysis: ClickHouse preferred for fast group-bys.
Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.corp/display/OBS/FVI+Design

2025-02-24: Security review requested: PII scrubber required in enrichment stage. Security flagged customer prompt fields; added requirement to strip or hash prompt snippets before persisting. (Security comment: SR-45).

2025-03-01: Dashboard mockups from design reviewed. UX requested inline quick-filter for model-version and route. Design PR attached.
Design mock: https://drive.google.com/designs/fvi-mock

2025-03-04: End-to-end smoke test in staging: anchors emitted for simulated timeout + model_reject flows; enrichment populated ClickHouse rows. Next: instrument A/B sampling to measure overhead and tune retention.
notes: Tradeoffs: full‑trace enrichment increases storage and cost. We will rely on a normalized FVI row (compact vector) for dashboards and keep full traces in sampling. This keeps SLO dashboards responsive while preserving investigatory traces for deep dives.

Failure taxonomy mapping: map HTTP 4xx -> client_error unless coupled with model_reject; HTTP 429 -> overload; gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED -> timeout; model-specific rejection codes come from model-response metadata (model_error, safety_reject).
Sampling strategy: 100% anchor emission at runtime, but only 10% of full traces persisted; all FVI rows are persisted to OLAP. This gives high signal coverage while bounding trace storage.

Operational runbooks will tie primary_reason -> suggested remediations: e.g., timeout -> increase request timeout, shift to lower-latency model variant, or isolate request sampling for debugging. Overload -> check instance queue depth/scale rules and backfill KV cache metrics.

Open question: how to represent 'compound' failures (e.g., model_reject following overloaded kernel causing partial outputs). Proposal: primary_reason = highest‑confidence root cause; secondary_reasons = list.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Anchor emission could add latency under p99 traffic. Mitigation: nonblocking append to trace buffer and feature flag to disable during emergency windows.
Risk: Sensitive customer data might be captured. Mitigation: enrichment stage runs PII scrubbing (regex + allowlist) and hashing for small prompt snippets before storing any text fields.

Risk: Noise from transient network errors inflating overload classification. Mitigation: require repeated error pattern (>=3 occurrences in 1 minute) to promote to 'overload' in the dashboard aggregation.
Risk: Model vendors use different rejection codes. Mitigation: maintain a model_adapters map to normalize vendor-specific codes into our taxonomy.
Risk: Schema churn for FVI table. Mitigation: use versioned schema with backward-compatibility columns and lightweight migration jobs.
implementation_plan: Task 1: Runtime hook (Aisha) - add error_anchor emit, feature-flagged, with unit tests. (PR: inference#4521)
Task 2: Kafka topic + Flink enrichment (Marco) - consume anchor events, enrich with route/model metadata, scrub PII, emit normalized FVI rows to ClickHouse.
Task 3: ClickHouse schema + retention (Data Eng) - create fvi_events table with TTL policy and rollup materialized views for 1h/1d aggregates.
Task 4: Grafana dashboards (SRE/Observability) - Fault Vector Overview, Route Drilldown, SLO correlation panels.
Task 5: Trace‑Anchor Playground UI (Frontend/Design) - list FVI rows, link to trace, annotate, and attach to incident. Minimal MVP: internal 1‑page app embedded in Console.
Task 6: Oncall runbooks mapping (PM/SRE) - map primary_reason -> canned remediation steps and attach to dashboard quick actions.
Task 7: Smoke tests + staging rollout (QA) - verify emission, enrichment, UI links, and PII scrubber effectiveness.
Task 8: Gradual rollout (Ops) - enable in staging, then 10% of production traffic, monitor p95 latency and storage growth; full rollout on success.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Cho): Ensure FVI is surfaced in customer-facing incident summaries where appropriate (obfuscated).
Design (K. Nguyen): Keep the Playground UI single-column, add quick filters for model_version and region.
Security (R. Gomez): Require automated PII scrubber in enrichment; provide logs-only mode for sensitive customers.
SRE (O. McBride): Prefer ClickHouse for fast aggregations; recommend 7-day hot window and 30-day cold rollups.
next_steps: Merge runtime PR behind feature flag and deploy to staging (target date: 2025-03-06).
Complete Flink enrichment pipeline and PII scrubber tests (target date: 2025-03-12).
Implement basic Grafana panels and internal Playground MVP (target date: 2025-03-18).
Coordinate a 10% production rollout and collect telemetry on overhead and signal usefulness (target date: 2025-03-25).
